summary.short: Bill adding GBL Article 45-A. From 1 January 2027, developers and deployers of high-risk AI decision systems used for consequential decisions about New York consumers must use reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination, with documentation, impact assessment and notice duties; the attorney general enforces it.
summary.long: The bill adds GBL Article 45-A, the AI Consumer Protection Act. It covers high-risk AI decision systems that make or substantially assist consequential decisions about New York consumers in listed areas such as education, employment, lending, housing, insurance, health care and essential government services. From 1 January 2027, developers must use reasonable care against known algorithmic discrimination risks, supply documentation to deployers and publish system statements; an independent audit creates a rebuttable presumption of reasonable care. Deployers must keep a risk management program, complete impact assessments annually and within 90 days of substantial modifications, notify consumers of consequential decisions, explain adverse decisions, allow correction and appeal, and publish a statement. Developers of general-purpose AI models must keep technical documentation. Persons must disclose AI interaction to consumers unless obvious. Exemptions cover certain federal approvals, insurers and banks deemed compliant, and specified research and security activities. The attorney general has exclusive enforcement authority, with a notice-and-cure period in 2027 and discretionary cure from 2028; violations are unfair trade practices under GBL § 349, and there is no private right of action.

notes: Excerpt of an introduced bill. The document contains only § 2 (adding GBL Article 45-A, §§ 1550-1556). The bill's section 1 and any effective-date provision are absent, and no version date is given. No enabling act or session-law relation is stated in the excerpt. Drafting defects: § 1555(3) opens with a malformed clause ('((b) pursuant to section seventy-nine-h'), with no closing clause (a). The defined term 'synthetic digital content' (§ 1550(15)) is not used in any operative provision. The 'general-purpose artificial intelligence model' definition (§ 1550(9)(a)) is built on the 'artificial intelligence decision system' definition, which is tied to consequential decisions.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment was found. The numbers in the text are dates (January 1, 2027 and 2028; January 1, 2026), procedural periods (ninety days in 1551(4)(b)(ii), 1552(3)(a)(ii)(B) and 1552(9); sixty days in 1556(2) and 1556(6)(a)(ii)), a record-retention period (three years in 1552(3)(e)), and the cure-period and record mechanics coded elsewhere, so they are not coded as thresholds. The definitions of consumer, consequential decision and high-risk system contain no numbers.
